doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Ginza live house and the Granz recording
title: The album title and the 'Toshiko's Blues' credit
summary: Brown reads the discography; she says the blues was really Bud Powell's tune and Granz's credit caused her trouble.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, I‟m looking at the discography entry for your … Amazing Toshiko
Akiyoshi. That‟s the title of the record [laughs].
Is it? No, Amazing, I don‟t think that was the one, though. I think the first one was a 10-inch [LP], the pink … the cover, [there was] a flower coming out of the piano.
Is that what it says, Amazing?
Well, that‟s what it is in this, this is the Tom Lord discography. It has the listing of tunes. First tune that is listed is “Toshiko‟s Blues.”
Because that is a Bud … a Bud … [sings] da-da-da-da-da-dahh, Bud played that one.
I think it‟s called “Bud‟s Blues” [composed by Sonny Stitt]. But probably he didn‟t copyright it.
So Norman gave me credit, which I got … you know, I needed that like a hole in the head, everybody thinks I stole it. But I had nothing to do with anything. That was really a drag.
